candidates.headline: Volatility at PSX, KSE-100 closes week lower
candidates.summary: Weekend wrap-up adding new detail to Friday's confirmed close already logged this cycle (KSE-100 171,021.20, -718.24/-718.25 pts, -0.42%): Business Recorder reports the session swung from an intraday low of 169,512.88 to a high of 172,718.66 before late profit-taking eroded the rally; index-heavy losers UBL, NBP, Systems Limited (SYS), HBL and FFC cumulatively cut about 436 points from the index. On a weekly basis the KSE-100 declined 2.7% (Business Recorder) / 2.72% (Express Tribune) WoW, attributed to 'continued escalation in tensions between the US and Iran' pushing crude oil prices higher and dampening investor sentiment. Express Tribune's read of the same Friday session adds breadth not previously logged (186 advancing, 270 declining, 36 unchanged) and stock-level detail: top gainers Adamjee Insurance (AICL) +6.38%, TRG Pakistan (TRG) +3.66%, Meezan Bank (MEBL) +0.3%; top losers NBP -2.18%, Systems Limited (SYS) -1.66%, UBL -1.2%; volume leader Cnergyico Pk (CNERGY) at 59.33m shares. Arif Habib Limited (AHL) quoted: the index 'has now fallen 10% from its July peak and is once again testing its 200-day moving average' - a bearish technical read not previously captured. Brent crude cited around $100/bbl on the same US-Iran/Red Sea escalation already logged this cycle; both outlets note markets are now looking ahead to the SBP's Monetary Policy Committee decision due July 27, 2026, widely expected (per the Topline Securities poll already logged) to hold the policy rate at 11.5% given the geopolitical and oil-price backdrop. No new price level beyond the already-logged 171,021.20 confirmed close; logged as impact 3 for the weekly-decline framing and the new AHL technical caution (200-day moving average test), which had not been captured in the prior daily-close entry.

candidates.headline: PSX surges over 5,000 points as US-Iran attacks pause and SBP rate-hold expectations lift sentiment
candidates.summary: Monday session (this checkpoint, from Friday's confirmed close of 171,021.20): Pakistan Observer reported the KSE-100 'gained 5,151 points in early trading session to climb to 176,172.20 points,' a positive change of 3.01 percent, citing Iranian military spokesperson Mohammad Reza Akraminia's statement that the US had suspended its attacks over the past two nights, prompting Iran to halt retaliatory operations, plus market anticipation that the State Bank of Pakistan's Monetary Policy Committee (meeting today, Jul 27) would keep the policy rate unchanged. PakTribune corroborated the same figures. PSX's own official market-summary page (psx.com.pk/market-summary/, captured 2026-07-27 12:25:02 PKT, market status 'Open') showed the index further extending to 176,284.99, up 5,263.79 points (+2.99%), volume 487,218,011 shares across 225,355 trades, breadth 430 advancing vs 56 declining. No SBP MPC decision had been announced as of this checkpoint (11:00-12:25 PKT); a prior Topline Securities poll (already logged Jul 21 and Jul 24) found 97% of respondents expect the rate held at 11.5%. Logged as impact 4 (sharp, market-wide geopolitical-driven move, >3% single-session swing) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10); escalation flagged. No individual stock-level figures independently verified in the sources reviewed beyond the index-wide move.

candidates.headline: KSE-100 confirmed Monday close: index surges over 7,200 points as US-Iran tensions ease and oil prices plunge
candidates.summary: Confirmed final close, from Friday's 171,021.20: Dawn reported the KSE-100 settled at 178,262.33 points, up 7,241.13 points (+4.23%), intraday peak 178,588.33, article published Jul 27, 2026, updated 04:54pm PKT. PSX's own market-summary page (psx.com.pk/market-summary/, captured 2026-07-27 17:40:01 PKT, market status 'Closed') showed the same 178,262.33 level and +7,241.13-point gain but a +4.06% change (percentage-basis discrepancy between the two sources, both quoted exactly as reported), volume 1,032,191,519 shares, 436,420 trades. Mettis Global's 'PSX Closing Bell: Good Times Roll' (mettisglobal.news/latest, published 04:33pm PKT) corroborated the greater-than-7,200-point surge, attributing it to 'easing geopolitical tensions and a sharp decline in global oil prices.' Drivers per Dawn: hopes for a US-Iran diplomatic resolution and resumption of Strait of Hormuz shipping; Brent crude fell over 7% to briefly dip below $90/barrel, WTI down 4% to $85.45; the State Bank of Pakistan held its policy rate at 11.5% (already logged this cycle). AKD Securities' Awais Ashraf called the SBP decision 'a cautious stance,' while predicting future rate cuts given a 'disinflationary trend, a comfortable external account position, weakening leading economic indicators.' Dawn reported that UBL, FFC, ENGROH, MEBL and LUCK collectively contributed approximately 2,546 points to the day's gain. Logged as impact 4 (sharp market-wide move, single-session index gain over 4%) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10); this is the confirmed final close superseding the intraday +5,263.79-point/+2.99% and +6,600.15-point/+3.86% reads already logged earlier this cycle.
